strongest_case: The shared-prefix three-arm design targets a real and currently unmeasured causal interface: whether a non-evidentiary typed frontier changes later bounded model computation enough to form a recipient-local public-witness connection. Byte-identical prefixes, no-feedback and same-kind distractor controls, frozen checkpoints, fresh calls, complete provenance, and postcommit scoring can make a negative or positive development result informative. The scientifically defensible recommendation is nevertheless REWORK TO OPTION C: do not reveal or answer the final paired goal; preserve raw model proposals and score exact requested-connection closure only after commitment. C is useful as an interface falsification and attribution study if it is described as query-guided witness binding, not autonomous discovery, and if compiler-only/query-copy controls, exchangeability checks, offline scoring, and complete call accounting are added. Option A is a legitimate later exploratory behavior experiment, but its answer and citations are not an entailing proof. Option B can be only a disclosed compiler/proof-kernel ceiling because its benchmark ontology and validator perform material reasoning. The exact current proposal is not launchable unchanged.

concerns.statement: The exact proposal cannot certify a mechanically supported final paired answer with the implemented thinker contract.
concerns.evidence: V03RPublicAgendaCompiler.compile_goal always emits a one-edge DIRECTED_PATH objective from source to target, including after the final question is revealed. That theorem returns the target entity and represents none of the role match, route/effect polarity, passive baseline, source contribution, subtraction-or-identity arithmetic, normalization, or workshop-label lookup required by lands.v03.parent_free_oracle. Existing tests explicitly label the release recurrence_probe_ceiling and final_goal_answer_scored=false.

concerns.statement: The proposed online admission/status channel is not attribution-neutral and is not yet non-generative across repeated calls.
concerns.evidence: The agenda exposes the exact left/relation/right tuple; V03RMechanicalSemanticAdmission recognizes a canonical route/effect grammar and promotes the generic edge; supported status is then model-visible. Rejected causal joins return no decision, so their absence can guide later retries, and no conclusion-level tombstone or no-retry invariant exists. The checker ignores the observed CHANGE/STABLE value when admitting causal_join, so it certifies connectivity rather than the effect-polarized object suggested by the final-task claim. The current admission tests exercise single-call mutations but not repeated adaptive proposals or status visibility. Under option C, raw proposals and citations should freeze before a blinded offline closure scorer runs; no admission outcome or reason should reach later cognition.

concerns.statement: Agenda success identifies query-guided evidence binding, not independent discovery or re-derivation of the relation identity.
concerns.evidence: canonical_target_blind_request serializes the complete requested left endpoint, causal_join relation, and right endpoint. The bounded selector ranks memory by exact atom overlap and lexical occurrence, while RETURN_SLEEP cycles the same public events regardless of arm. A model can copy the supplied tuple and cite compiler-shaped records. The existing bounded-view test proves locality but does not distinguish model reasoning from query copying plus deterministic retrieval/compiler assistance.

concerns.statement: The matched distractor is type-matched but not shown to be opportunity- or difficulty-matched to the own frontier.
concerns.evidence: The own and distractor joins can differ in route/effect positions, endpoint frequency, initial concept availability, bounded-memory rank, number of admissible witnesses, lexical overlap, and candidate-set size. Equal call counts do not make those closure opportunities exchangeable. Without precommit balance checks, agenda-minus-distractor can measure an easier tuple rather than goal-conditioned targeting.

concerns.statement: The current 1000-pair shortcut gate does not audit the bytes or feature joins exposed by the live recurrence interface.
concerns.evidence: lands.v03r._feature_components explicitly excludes valve-route joins and tests only lookup tables over goal, passive, effects, source, and role families. It does not train over raw rendered text, order/position, IDs, agenda coordinates, canonical route/effect strings, supported status, or combined route-effect/compiler features. A green passive gate therefore cannot establish that the live prompt and admission interfaces lack shortcuts.

concerns.statement: The named unit components do not yet compose into the exact six-life, heterogeneous-schedule, provider-bound experiment that the acceptance tests describe.
concerns.evidence: FrozenSchedule has one global expected_wake_calls/reactivation_calls pair, so the current scheduler cannot execute seed 0/2 at 46+22 and seed 1 at 49+24 in one run. HardenedThinkerMachineAdapter accepts a PolicyEmission and constructs a ledger from returned metadata rather than invoking IsolatedModelProviderBoundary; ScientificDreamAdapter is provider-bound but the recurrent scheduler consumes a separate dream() protocol. ImmutableExperimentCallLedger tests only a toy eight-slot schedule. The workflow-referenced preflight, runner, remote job, and test_v03r_live_text_transition files do not exist, so the frozen workflow correctly cannot advance but supplies no evidence for the proposed 802/288 reconciliation, reset isolation, recovery, or exact provider behavior.

concerns.statement: The full frozen job and its matched-compute interpretation are undefined because baseline physical schedules are not specified.
concerns.evidence: The 802 dream and at-most-288 thinker counts cover only recurrent conditions. Full transcript, iterative RAG, and wake-only baselines lack exact model-call slots, retrieval top-k/read counts, prompt and generation token envelopes, early-terminal accounting, and wall-time treatment. Under option C these baselines must be rewritten as closure/selection competitors; final-answer baselines belong to a later option-A intake.

concerns.statement: Hash reconciliation alone does not prove that every mandatory artifact exists.
concerns.evidence: verify_artifacts.py checks only paths enumerated by done.json; it has no independently frozen required-artifact inventory, schema, cardinality, or referential-integrity graph. A producer can omit an entire artifact class from done.json and still pass this verifier. The proposed deletion/orphan test requires an expected manifest rooted in reviewed inputs rather than in the producer's completion marker.

concerns.statement: Three aligned development pairs can route engineering decisions but cannot support reliability, robustness, or a general recurrence-effect claim.
concerns.evidence: The six lives are deliberately selected development seeds and share one model, skin, generator family, compiler, and tiny approximately 1.1k-token world. The 4/6, +2/6, and 2/3 gates are not confidence bounds. Any option-C report must present every paired outcome and call the result a development interface observation, including a null or control win, with no claim promotion or automatic follow-up.

visibility_failures: Do not expose admission success, failure, reason, or supported-status changes to any later dream in option C; score frozen raw proposals offline.
Do not describe the model-visible exact left/relation/right selection tuple as independently discovered content.
Do not allow a rejected or absent admission to become a retry signal; if online admission is ever retained, require one append-only conclusion-level attempt/tombstone with no adaptive feedback.
Do not let final-question, private twin, oracle, scorer, compiler-derived answer structure, provider-session state, or result-analysis state enter precommit cognition.
Do not treat a DERIVE validator or public-witness compiler as neutral model evidence; its vocabulary, responses, and computation are solver assistance.
missing_acceptance_tests: Option-C blinded offline closure: freeze raw proposals/citations first, mutate private/final truth without changing scorer inputs before commitment, and prove that no score or admission byte reaches cognition.
Adaptive admission attack: repeat, permute, and near-miss the same conclusion across all sixteen RETURN_SLEEP calls and prove no accept/reject bit, disappearance, rationale, or status enables search.

Compiler-attribution controls: no-model tuple copier, query-copy, masked-content, citation-permutation, wrong-connector, and canonical-string ablations with raw proposal and residual model contribution reported separately.
Own-versus-distractor exchangeability: precommit and test candidate-set size, witness count, endpoint frequency, event positions, bounded-memory rank, lexical overlap, and closure opportunity.

Heterogeneous full-job schedule: independently generate every six-life recurrent and baseline physical slot, prove one shared prefix per life, exact 802 recurrent dream calls, at most 288 recurrent thinker operations, and reconcile all baseline calls, reads, tokens, early terminals, and resets.
Independent artifact inventory: derive required file classes, cardinalities, IDs, and cross-references from frozen reviewed inputs rather than done.json, then reject omissions and orphans.

The workflow-named end-to-end transition, preflight, runner, and remote recovery tests must exist and prove their exact claims before immutable review; current generic component tests are not substitutes.
